pilgrimage_p1: Hi, Enda here... I'm walking around Europe on ancient pilgrim paths and visiting some Marian shrines along the way.
pilgrimage_p2: I live simply and stay at campsites or pilgrim shelters. While walking along I like to enjoy Nature and dedicate the pilgrimage to all those in ill-health.
shrine_panel_placeholder: Click a shrine for more info.
shrine_01_info1: On a rainy evening in 1879, villagers saw a vision of Our Lady shimmering beside a church wall.
shrine_01_info2: No words were spoken but this tiny village became a place of pilgrimage, drawing people in search of hope & peace.
shrine_02_info1: According to tradition, a noblewoman in the 11th century received a vision of Mary’s home in Nazareth.
shrine_02_info2: The Holy House built here in rural Norfolk became one of medieval Europe’s great pilgrimage destinations.
shrine_03_info1: In 1933, Mariette Beco reported a vision of Our Lady by a garden spring. Mary invited people to visit & pray for the poor.
shrine_03_info2: The flowing waters give Banneux a calm atmosphere among the hills of eastern Belgium.
shrine_04_info1: In 1858, Bernadette Soubirous reported visions of Our Lady at the grotto of Massabielle
shrine_04_info2: Since then, generations of sick and injured pilgrims have visited these holy waters seeking healing and hope.
shrine_05_info1: In a riverside basilica stands a pillar of jasper stone, said to have been left behind by Our Lady.
shrine_05_info2: According to tradition, Mary appeared here while still living in Jerusalem, to encourage St James in his mission.
shrine_06_info1: In 1917, three shepherd children reported visions of Our Lady near the village of Aljustrel.
shrine_06_info2: The events transformed this rural landscape & every evening thousands gather with candles at this vast sanctuary.
shrine_07_info1: The Shrine of 'Our Lady of Europe' stands on the Rock of Gibraltar, where the Mediterranean meets the Atlantic.
shrine_07_info2: For centuries, sailors paused to pray at this gateway between continents.
shrine_08_info1: Overlooking the Adriatic stands the 'Holy House' of Nazareth; the building where Mary received the Annunciation.
shrine_08_info2: Legend says it was carried here during the Middle Ages from Nazareth, and today the basilica is a world-wide attraction.
shrine_09_info1: On Malta’s northern coast, candlelit chapels and stone passages lead down towards the sea.
shrine_09_info2: Tradition links Mellieħa to early Christianity where some believe St Luke visited the cave beneath the church.
shrine_10_info1: Deep in the Swiss Alps, a wooden statue of the Black Madonna is honoured in the Chapel of Grace.
shrine_10_info2: For a thousand years, pilgrims have been visiting this Abbey, where Monks still pray beneath its painted ceilings.
shrine_11_info1: The small octagonal chapel at Altötting holds a revered image of Our Lady.
shrine_11_info2: Its walls are covered with painted testimonies of healing and gratitude from pilgrims down the ages.
shrine_12_info1: Legend tells of a monk carrying a statue of Mary who prayed here when a rock blocked his path.
shrine_12_info2: The rock split open and in time the small wooden statue became the heart of Mariazell basilica.
shrine_13_info1: Beneath the Julian Alps lies Slovenia’s most important pilgrimage site & a place of comfort during hardship.
shrine_13_info2: In 1883, a fire damaged much of the church, but the famous image of 'Mary Help of Christians' survived unharmed.
shrine_14_info1: The shrine is known for its Black Madonna statue, hidden for centuries during invasion and unrest.
shrine_14_info2: After it was rediscovered, Marija Bistrica became Croatia’s leading pilgrimage site and long processions still fill its streets.
shrine_15_info1: This Greek Catholic basilica on the plains of eastern Hungary is often filled with insence and chanting.
shrine_15_info2: It became famous in the 17th century after an icon of Mary was said to weep tears.
shrine_16_info1: According to tradition, a spring began to flow here after a miraculous healing many centuries ago.
shrine_16_info2: Today, forest paths lead visitors through the hills of northern Hungary to this holy well.
shrine_17_info1: Every July, crowds gather on Marian Hill above this medieval town for one of Slovakia’s great pilgrimages.
shrine_17_info2: Pilgrims have climbed the hillside since the 13th century, when local people found refuge during the Mongol invasions.
shrine_18_info1: Every Pentecost, pilgrims cross the mountains of Transylvania to gather at this open-air shrine.
shrine_18_info2: At the heart of the sanctuary stands a famous carved statue of Mary.
shrine_19_info1: The image of the Black Madonna, marked by scars and centuries of history, is a symbol of hope for Poland.
shrine_19_info2: Every summer, thousands of pilgrims walk to the fortified monastery carrying banners, flowers, and prayers.
shrine_20_info1: Above an ancient gate in the old town stands the Shrine of 'Our Lady of the Gate of Dawn'.
shrine_20_info2: For centuries, prayer and candlelight have filled the small chapel overlooking the streets below.
shrine_21_info1: According to tradition, a monk fleeing invasion discovered an icon of Mary after falling asleep beneath some trees.
shrine_21_info2: Today, pilgrims follow paths through western Ukraine to reach the healing waters of this Greek Catholic shrine.
